The Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution law for molecules of mass $m$ at temperature $T$ is given by:
$$dN(v) = 4\pi N \left(\frac{m}{2\pi k_B T}\right)^{3/2} v^2 e^{-mv^2 / 2k_B T} dv$$

The average speed $\langle v \vbar$ (or $\bar{v}$) is calculated as:
$$\langle v \rangle = \frac{\int_{0}^{\infty} v \, dN(v)}{N} = 4\pi \left(\frac{m}{2\pi k_B T}\right)^{3/2} \int_{0}^{\infty} v^3 e^{-mv^2 / 2k_B T} dv$$

Using the standard integral formula $\int_{0}^{\infty} x^3 e^{-ax^2} dx = \frac{1}{2a^2}$, where $a = \frac{m}{2k_B T}$:
$$\langle v \rangle = 4\pi \left(\frac{m}{2\pi k_B T}\right)^{3/2} \left[ \frac{1}{2 \left(\frac{m}{2k_B T}\right)^2} \right] = \sqrt{\frac{8 k_B T}{\pi m}} = \sqrt{\frac{8 R T}{\pi M}}$$
proTip: Memorize standard Gaussian/gamma integrals to quickly evaluate average and root-mean-square speeds in exams.
